overview_initial:
Draw a NEW, simplified, accurate academic schematic titled "FSDR and RACE in LViT". Reference image is for VISUAL STYLE ONLY: white paper, pastel blue 3D feature cuboids, orange RACE blocks, green FSDR decoder blocks, elegant serif labels, thin arrows. High resolution landscape. No performance numbers and no BetterLViT name.
Exactly TWO U-shaped branches side by side:
LEFT ViT U: four blue Down ViT blocks, top-to-bottom labelled 1,2,3,4; four blue Up ViT blocks ascending, TOP-to-BOTTOM labelled 1,2,3,4. Blue encoder arrows descend, decoder arrows ascend, bottom U link. Each Up ViT has a short output port, TOP-to-BOTTOM V1,V2,V3,V4.
RIGHT CNN U: Image input DIRECTLY ABOVE C1, aligned with it. Downward blue encoder column C1,C2,C3,C4, bottom bottleneck C5. To its right, FOUR orange lateral RACE blocks. To their right, FOUR green decoder-stage blocks, top-to-bottom labelled "up1", "up2", "up3", "up4". INSIDE each green block print "FSDR fusion". At every row: C_i -> RACE_i -> green up_i, label connecting arrow C'_i. CNN downward path branches BEFORE RACE. C5 -> bottom green up4 -> up3 -> up2 -> up1 -> output infection mask. THIS ordinary U chain is enough, no extra unlabeled decoder blocks, no separate upsample boxes. Each green block contains the WHOLE up stage. Below the diagram write the exact stage definition: "Each up stage: Upsample → FSDR → Concat(Y, D') → Conv ×2".
Above or next to each green up-stage block place a SHORT INPUT PORT labelled V1,V2,V3,V4 respectively, top-to-bottom. The lowest port MUST say V4, not V3. Do not draw long ViT-to-CNN wires; matching labels denote the same features. Legend "V_i: reconstructed feature from the matching Up ViT level".
Above left, Report -> Frozen CXR-BERT -> small port T. Then caption "T conditions ViT, RACE and FSDR". NO long T bus and NO T arrow into CNN encoder. Caption "C_i also guides the matching Down ViT level" with short C_i ports if needed.
No PLAM blocks. Caption "FSDR replaces PLAM; RACE refines decoder-bound skips".
No tensor shapes, H/n sizes, random extra labels or dummy dangling arrows. Avoid chest image thumbnail if it complicates arrows; an input cuboid labelled "CXR image" is sufficient. Output simple cuboid labelled "Infection mask".

fsdr:
Draw a NEW standalone academic scientific architecture diagram titled "FSDR: semantic and detail refinement". White background, pastel blue 3D feature-map cuboids, muted green operation nodes, clean arrows and serif labels, large readable text. Landscape. Reference is VISUAL STYLE ONLY. No unrelated RACE model or numeric results.
Use MATCHING SIGNAL PORTS to avoid crossing wires. Split into a LARGE TOP main graph and a SMALL BOTTOM adaptive subgraph. They exchange values by identically named ports, not long connecting wires.

TOP MAIN GRAPH, left to right:
Input C* splits BEFORE any operation: one identity bypass goes around top border to the final ADD circle; one goes to "Haar split". Haar has outputs C_low and C_high.
C_low enters a green "Semantic refinement" operation. Three additional short input ports immediately beside it are labelled V_low, D'_low, T. All three arrows enter Semantic refinement directly. T must not connect to Haar or D'_low.
Semantic refinement has two outputs: upper R_sem goes DIRECTLY into final ADD; lower "Support S" goes to green "Detail refinement". C_high independently goes into Detail refinement. Its subtitle is "Local + context conv". Detail output αd R_detail goes DIRECTLY into final ADD.
One additional small input port R_adaptive beside the ADD enters it.
ADD has exactly four inputs: ORIGINAL C* identity, R_sem, αd R_detail, R_adaptive. Its output is Y.
This is all of the top graph. DO NOT draw Concat or decoder convolution here.

BOTTOM ADAPTIVE SUBGRAPH, dashed boundary "up4 / up3 only":
Input ports C_low,V_low,D_low -> "Spatial mixture weights" -> "Adaptive low/high-pass". Two separate output cubes D' and R_adaptive, with short ending arrows/ports. They DO NOT connect to one another and DO NOT use physical wires into the top graph; matching names identify values. Small note "D'_low = Haar low(D')".
Under bottom subgraph print "up2 / up1: D' = D, R_adaptive = 0".
At bottom-right, simply label "Module outputs: Y and D' → decoder concatenation". This is a text interface note, not a connecting wire.

Equations in footer:
"R_sem = αp V_low + R_channel + αr R_region"
"Y = C* + R_sem + αd R_detail + R_adaptive"
"C* = routed C' with RACE, otherwise C"

NO shape annotations, no invented operations. Preserve the independent C* bypass and separate semantic and detail residuals. Every arrow accurate. Use generous whitespace.
race_initial:
Academic architecture diagram on a pure white background. Match the supplied LViT figure's pastel blue/lavender 3D feature-map cuboids, colored operation blocks, thin clean arrows and restrained serif labels. Publication quality, high-resolution landscape, spacious, precise short English labels, no black slide background, no dashboard. No BetterLViT name. Image is a manual draw.io reference. Do not copy the original PLAM inset.
Create ONLY a standalone RACE internal architecture diagram, titled "RACE: report–anatomy consistency and evidence fusion". Orange operation nodes and blue feature cuboids. Spacious LEFT TO RIGHT graph. No overall architecture and no FSDR panel.
Use exactly the following dependencies. Named signal ports can replace long crossing wires.
1. T (frozen text) -> Masked mean -> Slot head -> six location scores z.
2. z and a SEPARATE fixed Six-zone basis B are two distinct incoming arrows into "Spatial prior P". DO NOT draw z -> B.
3. CNN skip C -> "Visual evidence E". E plus B -> "Zone pooling". Pooled evidence plus z -> "Agreement A".
4. Three inputs P, E, A -> node labelled "G = P × E × A". E must feed this gate directly in addition to the separate zone-pooling path.
5. CNN skip C independently -> "Residual R(C)" with subtitle "DWConv 3×3 + PWConv 1×1". R(C) is learned convolutions, NEVER C - E.
6. R(C) and gate G feed a node labelled "s G ⊙ R(C)" (the scalar s is learned).
7. ORIGINAL C takes an identity bypass around the bottom margin and enters a large PLUS circle. The only other PLUS input is the output of "s G ⊙ R(C)". PLUS -> C' (routed skip).
The identity bypass must enter ONLY the PLUS, NEVER the gate or scaled residual. No extra multiplication circles anywhere.
Bottom formula exactly "C' = C + s G ⊙ R(C)".
Small note "|s| ≤ 0.15; zero at initialization".
Training-only note in a small dashed annotation, NOT in inference data flow: "Auxiliary supervision trains report slots and visual evidence".
Use clearly labeled short input ports P/E/A/z/B as necessary to prevent line crossings. Arrows must not cross node interiors or text. No tensor shapes, no invented full-name expansion beyond the title above.
race_final_edit:

Instead, place a small input label "z" immediately ABOVE "Agreement A" and draw a short downward arrow from this z label into Agreement A. The z is the same six location scores produced by the Slot head; a named matching port is sufficient, no long crossing wire.
